title: Automated overage heuristics and post-invoice adjustment runbook
creator: Aisha Raman
description: Problem: Enterprise customers occasionally submit security questionnaire responses or contract amendments that change metering boundaries mid-billing-cycle (e.g., excluding certain internal traffic, temporarily suspending a project, or accepting a provisional credit during incident remediation). Our current billing flow requires manual reconciliation which causes delayed credits, disagreements, and higher support overhead. Goal: Define an automated heuristic layer and a clear post-invoice adjustment runbook that reduces manual interventions by at least 60%, ensures auditable adjustments, and integrates with contracts/security questionnaire gates for faster resolution.
acceptance_criteria: A1: System proposes automated adjustment candidates for >= 80% of common overage cases (incident credits, mid-cycle exclusions, duplicate metering) with confidence score and rationale.

A2: Generated adjustments include an auditable reason, origin link (PR/contract/Support ticket), and proposed credit amount; ops can approve with a single click or schedule automatic apply for low-risk cases.
A3: Adjustments are surfaced in the Billing Console timeline and through the finance webhook with idempotency keys and invoice references.
A4: Runbook documents step-by-step manual reconciliation for high-risk or disputed adjustments and includes SLA for customer response and finance posting.
A5: Metrics dashboard shows reduction in manual credits, time-to-credit median, and dispute reopen rate; baseline and target documented.
A6: Security questionnaire exceptions that affect metering are gated and require entry in the audit log; changes cannot be auto-applied without security_review_required flag set to false.
implementation_notes: Design a candidate generator service that consumes metering deltas, incident tags (from PagerDuty/ops-ticket), contract amendment flags, and security-questionnaire exceptions.
Confidence model heuristics: historical similar adjustments, contract clause presence, incident severity, customer tier, and manual override frequency.

Store proposed adjustments as Records in the Adjustment Ledger with fields: invoice_id, candidate_amount, rationale_text, origin_link, confidence_score, proposed_by(service/agent), status(proposed/approved/applied/rejected).
Expose an ops UI in Console -> Billing -> Adjustments with bulk approve for low-risk candidates and a secure approval flow for high-risk ones requiring finance + PM signoff.

APIs: POST /billing/adjustments/propose, GET /billing/adjustments?status=proposed, POST /billing/adjustments/{id}/apply, POST /billing/adjustments/{id}/reject. Webhooks for applied adjustments and invoice updates.

Financial posting: applied adjustments must create a ledger entry that reconciles with the invoice and produces a credit memo; integrate with Stripe/GCP billing connector for automatic credit application where supported.
Audit & retention: keep full rationale and source artifacts (linked docs) for 7 years; tie to contract id and security-questionnaire id for enterprise compliance requests.
Fallback: if auto-apply fails or customer disputes, runbook instructs ops to open a provisional-payment hold and escalate to finance for manual journal entry.
Telemetry: add metrics for candidate precision/recall, apply success rate, median time from proposal to apply, and reduction in support tickets referencing billing disputes.
risks: Overly aggressive auto-applies may create incorrect credits and financial leakage.
Security questionnaire exceptions may be misinterpreted without human review; must preserve manual gate for high-risk customers.
Integration gaps with external payment processors could delay credit memo issuance.
mitigations: Start with read-only proposals and 'ops approve' flow for 6 weeks before allowing auto-apply for low-risk patterns.
Require security_review_required flag for any adjustments originating from security questionnaire changes.
Add idempotency keys and strong validation against invoice totals before applying credits.
